note: Private mutation/regression corpus for SwiftInferProperties — the inference engine dogfooding on itself (Chapter 30 §30.4.4). Two families: mutants in the IdempotenceWitnessDetector's own name-classifier, and mutants that undo a name-only-position guard (a key-path component's or a member's name read as a test-local). Each is killed by its own code's unit tests, which pin both what it should and should not do. Run via `swift test --filter`. Not a scored benchmark.

mutants.label: drop `reset` from the exact-name set — a genuinely idempotent action is no longer recognized as a witness
add `increment` to the exact-name set — a non-idempotent action is falsely classified as an idempotence witness
drop the `set` prefix — `setX`-style assignments are no longer recognized as prefix-match witnesses
ReceiverConstructionHarvester's free-name check skips member names only — `\.name` reads as a test-local and `Sorter(by: \.name)` is never harvested
ReceiverConstructionHarvester's inliner rewrites key-path names — `let pageSize = 10` harvests `Pager(sortedBy: \.10, pageSize: 10)`
the Slicer's identifier collector records member and key-path names — `.map(\.id)` and `{ $0.id }` pull an unrelated `let id = 7` into the property region
LocalBindingResolver substitutes into a key-path name — `let id = makeID()` makes `\.makeID()`, a component whose declName slot holds a call
MinedTraceSelector counts every lowercase name as a test-local — `Feature.State(color: .red)` and `Feature.State(sort: \.name)` are dropped
